title: The Regiment of Manchester's mill district
premise: In 1848 Manchester, Marguerite Sandoval works in her father's print shop, cutting type and keeping the shop's ledger of debts, names, and favors for the mill district's immigrant families. When the army requisitions the town to crush the Chartist uprisings, the ledger becomes evidence of sedition—and the only record of who deserves passage on the last barge out of the district. Marguerite must decide whether to burn the names or save them, knowing either choice condemns someone she loves. She ultimately gives the final berth to a stranger's orphaned child instead of her own brother, forging a found family among the left-behind who rebuild the print shop as a press for the resistance.
about_author: Sebastian Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing Victorian industrial records in northern England before turning to fiction. His novels examine how ordinary people survive when institutions turn against them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Marguerite Sandoval cuts type by lamplight in her father's print shop, measuring her world in what can be carried: letters, ledger entries, her mother's rosary. POV Marguerite. Establishes the rhythm of the district and her quiet competence. Emotional beat: contentment built on fragile routines.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Marguerite balances the shop's ledger, which secretly records every family's debts, births, and allegiances in the mill district. Her brother Tomás mocks its sentimentality. POV Marguerite with a brief interlude from Tomás. Emotional beat: sibling friction over what loyalty means.

chapters.title: Red Flags Over Ancoats
chapters.summary: Chartist agitators hold a meeting in the print shop after hours; Marguerite prints handbills she pretends not to read. Father Sandoval warns her to stay invisible. POV Marguerite. Emotional beat: the intoxicating pull of belonging to something larger.

chapters.title: The Requisition
chapters.summary: Soldiers occupy the district at dawn, posting orders on the shop door. An officer requisitions the building as a garrison office and demands all business records—including the ledger. POV Marguerite. Emotional beat: cold dread replacing routine.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Knows
chapters.summary: Father burns some pages but Marguerite has memorized the rest. The officer, Captain Ellery, is courteous and watchful, suspecting more than he says. POV alternating Marguerite and Ellery. Emotional beat: the terror of being truly seen.

chapters.title: Names Are Evidence
chapters.summary: A neighbor is arrested because his name appears in the ledger. Families beg Marguerite to remove their entries; she cannot without alerting Ellery. POV Marguerite. Emotional beat: guilt—the keeper of names becomes their betrayer.

chapters.title: Tomás Disappears
chapters.summary: Tomás joins the barricade builders and vanishes during a sweep. Marguerite searches the holding pens, bribing a soldier with type metal melted into ingots. POV Marguerite. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Barge List
chapters.summary: Ellery announces evacuation: one barge will carry forty residents to safety before the district is sealed. Selection will be made from official records—unless someone can prove need. POV Ellery, revealing his own doubts. Emotional beat: hope entangled with bureaucratic cruelty.

chapters.title: Forty Berths, Four Hundred Souls
chapters.summary: The district descends into bargaining and betrayal as families lobby for places. Marguerite realizes her memory of the ledger makes her the true arbiter. POV Marguerite. Emotional beat: the corrupting weight of power she never wanted.

chapters.title: The Widow Okafor's Bargain
chapters.summary: Widow Okafor offers Marguerite her late husband's hidden savings for two berths—for herself and any child but her sickly grandson. Marguerite refuses the money but cannot stop thinking about it. POV Marguerite. Emotional beat: shame at what desperation makes of people.

chapters.title: Midnight Inventory
chapters.summary: Marguerite inventories everything she can carry and confronts what each object costs to abandon. Father collapses; his heart is failing and he needs the berth most medically. POV Marguerite. Emotional beat: grief rehearsed in advance.

chapters.title: Ellery's Offer
chapters.summary: Ellery privately offers Marguerite three berths in exchange for the ledger's seditious pages and the name of the Chartists' printer. He suspects it is her father—or her. POV Ellery. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Printer's Mark
chapters.summary: Marguerite discovers the resistance has been using her own discarded type slugs to print pamphlets; her craft is already complicit. She meets the underground printer, a girl named Ada. POV Ada. Emotional beat: recognition—she was never invisible.

chapters.title: Tomás Found
chapters.summary: Tomás resurfaces, wounded, hiding in the cellar. Sheltering him makes every family member guilty if discovered. Marguerite must count berths again: father, brother, herself—one too few. POV Marguerite. Emotional beat: love as arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Burning Question
chapters.summary: Father urges Marguerite to trade the ledger for three berths; Tomás urges her to give it to the resistance as a weapon. The ledger sits between them like a third child. POV Marguerite. Emotional beat: the family fracturing over survival's price.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: During a raid, Widow Okafor is shot leaving her grandson, six-year-old Emile, on the shop step. Marguerite takes him in without deciding to. POV Marguerite. Emotional beat: compassion arriving before strategy.

chapters.title: The Count Changes
chapters.summary: With Emile hidden upstairs, the arithmetic becomes unbearable: four people, three berths. Tomás volunteers to stay and fight; Marguerite refuses to let him be a martyr for her conscience. POV Tomás. Emotional beat: brotherhood tested against self-sacrifice.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Carries
chapters.summary: She forges official passes using her type-cutting skill—a hanging offense—making a fourth berth exist that never did. Ellery nearly catches her mid-forgery. POV Marguerite. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: The Last Barge
chapters.summary: At the loading dock, chaos and bayonets. Marguerite surrenders her own berth so Emile can board, giving Ellery the forged pass with her name scratched out. POV Ellery watching her choose. Emotional beat: sacrifice as identity finally claimed.

chapters.title: The Officer's Silence
chapters.summary: Ellery finds the real ledger page naming the printer—Ada—and burns it himself, then looks away as the barge departs overloaded. His reasons remain his own. POV Ellery. Emotional beat: a compromised man choosing one clean act.

chapters.title: Left Behind
chapters.summary: Marguerite, Tomás, and the remaining families seal themselves in the print shop as the district burns. They pull the press from the rubble and set type by firelight. POV Marguerite. Emotional beat: devastation becoming foundation.

chapters.title: First Impression
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the rebuilt press runs its first sheet: a list of every name from the ledger, printed so none are forgotten. Marguerite, no longer invisible, reads it aloud to her found family. POV Marguerite. Emotional beat: survival transformed into witness.
